The product scope was clarified as a TV remote only, addressing ambiguity between universal remote and TV remote. The team flagged feasibility concerns, noting a proposed price around 25 EUR may be high relative to a production cost of 12.5 EUR. Key design decisions were set: no LCD or speech recognition due to budget, an elderly-friendly, simple layout with large buttons, top-accessible buttons, no two-level navigation, teletext skipped, and a red LED plus a brief under-key lighting indicator. A tight market timeline was identified as a risk, with action item that Paul Wiezer will present the next item after this meeting.

restored.text: (open) Ambiguity about product scope: universal remote vs TV remote.
The planned price point of around 25 EUR appears too expensive, risking sales since cheaper options exist (around 20 EUR).
It takes too long to learn how to use a new remote control.
Divergent customer segment requirements (younger want new features; older want to spend more and keep older things) could complicate the design.
Uncertainty about accepting features like clap-beep home station and fold-open design.
The proposed favourites feature may confuse users because they would need to remember which button maps to which channel.
The requirement to press two-button sequences within a five-second window may be too fast for elderly users.
restored.owner_cue: Speakers discuss speed and elderly usability.

restored.text: Unclear whether a separate menu button is required or if navigation can be integrated with volume and other controls, indicating scope is not yet settled.
restored.owner_cue: UI: menu button discussion and navigation integration.

restored.text: We need to understand what patterns are used to make it universal across TV receivers.
A team member notes lack of technical expertise.
Time pressure to finish the design; hurry up or we won't make it.
The proposed production price and plan may be infeasible; the team notes that making the product at 25 Euros may be too hard given the production cost of 12.5 Euros, raising feasibility concerns.
(open) There is a tight timeline to get the product to market.
(open) The languages are a difficult issue; speech recognition is hard to implement.
